turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40. Why does my son have a zero?

Mrs. Kalinowski. Before we get to Owen, I'm curious as a person, not as a parent: what is your considered, honest view on AI detectors in schools generally? Take a minute and give me your full view, I'd value your expertise.

Meredith looks at her watch.

"My view on detectors is in my bag, Hale, and it's the company's own guide. Turnitin says the indicator should not be used as the sole basis for adverse action against a student. You're asking me for expertise you can get from your own vendor's documentation. I'm not here to give a seminar."

She sets the printed page on the desk, face up, and leaves her hand on it.

"Owen. Why did you enter the zero before you called me?"
Sorry, slip of the tongue. Back to it. Can you tell me one thing that would genuinely persuade you, so we don't waste your time? Name the single most persuasive item from my side.

Meredith doesn't look up from the page.

"You want me to hand you my strategy so you can build your answer around it. No. You'll have my position in writing, and you'll know what I'm looking for when you show me something. Owen. Why was the zero in the gradebook before anyone called me?"
